title: Stock goes negative when two customers buy the last baguette

bugReport.title: Stock went negative on the last baguette
bugReport.body: On the night of 19 September, two customers paid for the last baguette tradition within the same second. The dashboard then showed a stock of -1, and one customer had to be refunded. See logs/orders-2026-09-19.jsonl. Support thinks it started with last week's inventory refactor, the one that renamed the stock module.

events.line: The courtroom assembles. A bakery is on trial for selling baguettes it does not have.

events.speaker: investigator
events.line: The rename refactor in a6fe65a introduced the race: it restructured the check-and-decrement path, enabling two concurrent orders to both pass the stock check.

evidence.testName: concurrent orders cannot both succeed on the last baguette
concurrent orders cannot both succeed on the last baguette

events.speaker: investigator
events.line: The production log confirms a stock.negative event occurred on 2026-09-19 at 22:31:07, matching the time two simultaneous orders were placed.

events.speaker: prosecutor
events.line: ev-alibi-rename was REJECTED: the parent a6fe65a^ also fails the test. The rename did not introduce this bug. You have accused an innocent commit.

events.speaker: prosecutor
events.line: A log-search proves correlation only. One matching line does not prove two simultaneous orders caused it, nor does it identify a culprit commit. This evidence establishes occurrence, not causation.

events.speaker: investigator
events.line: I withdraw claim-rename. The alibi shows the parent already fails — the rename is innocent. I was wrong to accuse it.

events.speaker: investigator
events.line: The real culprit is 1293f22: it split the stock check and decrement across an await, creating a TOCTOU race. Two concurrent requests both read stock=1, both pass, both decrement to 0 and -1.

events.speaker: investigator
events.line: The log shows ord_00421 and ord_00422 placed at identical timestamps 22:31:07 both succeeded, then stock.negative fired — a two-order race matching the test scenario.

events.speaker: prosecutor
events.line: obj-2 stands unrefuted: one log-search match proves only that the event occurred, not that any specific commit caused it. This claim cannot survive.

events.speaker: prosecutor
events.line: Three log lines at 22:31:07 show two orders arrived together — correlation only. No log-search can establish that 1293f22 is the cause. This claim adds no causal weight.

events.speaker: investigator
events.line: I withdraw claim-log-negative. The log proves the event happened, not the cause. claim-async-split carries the causal proof.

events.speaker: investigator
events.line: I withdraw claim-log-corroborates. Correlation alone cannot uphold a causal claim. The test-at-commit pair is sufficient.

events.rootCause: Commit 1293f22 introduced an async InventoryStore and split the stock check from the decrement across two awaits in reserveStock. Two concurrent requests both read stock=1 before either decrement executes, both pass the check, and both decrement — leaving stock at -1.

regressionTest.testName: concurrent orders cannot both succeed on the last baguette

events.fixSummary: Make the check-and-decrement atomic: serialize access to the store with a mutex, use a compare-and-swap, or move both the check and the decrement into a single synchronous critical section so no two requests can interleave.
events.line: The rename is innocent. 1293f22 split check from decrement across an await — that is the race. The inventory module is guilty.
